identification: Three containers: a wooden box of mixed world coins (mostly modern foreign), a plastic tub with Australian KGV/KGVI pennies and halfpennies, a Tudor-rose florin, a holed large medal or crown, gilt pins, cufflinks and knapped flint or chert flakes, and a shoebox of predecimal pennies, halfpennies, a QEII crown and world coins. Mostly common circulated copper and cupronickel. Photos cannot show dates, so any 1946-or-earlier silver florins or half crowns, or a key-date penny (1919 dot, 1930, 1946), is unconfirmed.

viewing_check: Sort the pennies by date: look for 1919 dot, 1930, 1925, 1923, 1946/47 and any Edward VII or Victoria pennies. Check every florin and half crown for a date of 1946 or earlier (silver, magnet-free, ring tone) and any pre-1920 .925 silver. Check the holed medal or crown for a date and maker, and whether the stone points are real worked artefacts with provenance.
